On 9th April I took three Core positional entries: Syrma, Valiant &  Waaree Energies.
Syrma is up +110%.
Valiant is up +57%.
Waaree went against me. I booked the SL at -12%. 
It is down 20% today.
Basket return: ~+51%.
Two winners carried one loser .
This is how Core investing actually works. Out of every 10 positions, around 3 or 4 will fail. That is normal. 
Job is simple. Keep losers small. Let one or two big winners run properly. 
Look at the maths. One stock up 110% covers nine exits at -12%. One winner. Nine losers. You are still in profit.
Core parameters to screen - Earnings explosion with Sharp YoY acceleration. Price confirming the earnings. Basically, PEAD structure.

Market Commentary:

Yet another stress test day, which both the SPY and QQQ passed as it gapped into support and reversed higher. Positive news catalysts mid-day contributed to the upside action as well, with many AI related names finding intraday support and closed higher. While market breadth has indeed continue to deteriorate, leadership continues to decouple and remain strong - arguing for the case of a strengthening market under the hood.

Looking at the dollar, price is now 'mid-air' as it approaches prior left side peaks (LSP) established in June-July 2026. 

Precious metals in relation continue to struggle, with Gold living below all relevant moving averages, while Silver trades sandwiched betwen the looming 10/20-EMA, and 50-SMA which acts as support for now.

Constructive action overall in cryptoland, as the majors (BTC/ETH/SOL) found buyers at/near the rising 10-EMA after breaking out on Monday.

Cross asset action in the overnight session argues for a risk-on environment brewing - slightly reminiscent of late April - May 2025.

Notes:

> We finally got a 2-day pullback from a 4-day ripper higher in QQQ. Price action and the action in leadership has remained constructive and passed the stress test.

> Looking at leadership, many names are now quietly consolidating on constructive price/volume dynamics. Additional follow through the potential for a risk-on momentum environment increases.

> Net new lows continue to expand, but market breadth across different MAs trading at the lower end of the ranges argue for the potential that a flip higher becoming the spark that triggers a risk-on move.

The most underrated concept in trading:

Opportunity cost.

Most traders focus on the loss they're sitting in.
They should be focused on the profit they're missing.

Here's what I mean.

You hold a losing position for 2 months.
It's down 20%. You're "waiting for it to come back."

But what actually happened in those 2 months?

Your capital was locked.
You couldn't act on anything.
You watched setups come and go.
You missed the move you actually saw coming.

Now flip it.

You followed your plan. Stop hit at -5%. You moved on.
That 5% is recoverable in a week on the right trade.
The capital is free to work again.
You're in control.
The position didn't just cost you 20%.
It cost you every single trade you couldn't take while you were in it.

That's opportunity cost.

Once you start thinking about your capital as a tool - not something to protect your ego with - trading stops being a hobby.

It becomes a business.

If you're struggling to take losses, save this and read this everytime you feel the need to.

🐼 Why the Panda?

If you’re new here, you’ll quickly notice we talk a lot about the Patient Panda.

It started as a simple analogy, but over time it became one of the central ideas behind how we approach trading in PrimeTrading.

Patience is one of the hardest skills to build as a trader, and it shows up in a few different ways.

1. When the market is not good

You don’t need to force trades just because you’re sitting in cash.

Sometimes there simply isn’t a good pitch.

The absence of opportunity is not a signal to act. It’s a signal to conserve capital, conserve mental energy, and wait for the environment to improve.

That’s Panda Mode.

2. When you’re already in a position

Even great trades don’t move in a straight line.

There will be pullbacks, retests, red days and periods where the stock goes nowhere.

The skill is staying composed and letting the position work as long as the trend and structure remain intact.

A lot of traders do the hard part correctly — they find the right stock and get the right entry — then kill their own edge by becoming impatient and selling too early.

3. When executing the plan

Patience also means sticking to the process.

Trim into strength at your predetermined targets. Hold exposure when the trend still supports it. Don’t completely change your plan because of one uncomfortable candle.

You don’t get paid for being constantly active.

You get paid for executing well when the opportunity is there, and then having the patience to let that edge play out.

As Jesse Livermore said:

“It was never my thinking that made the big money for me. It always was my sitting.”

That’s really the essence of Patient Panda.

It’s not just a mascot or an inside joke. It’s a reminder to:

Be patient. Stay composed. Stop forcing action. Let the market come to you. 🐼
